precepts.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. So the valley of the shadow of death is the same darkness that Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. That is the valley he is talking about.
precepts.point: Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. That is the unity Malcolm was talking about. That unity of us standing together, standing as one, in one mind, one understanding, one God, one race, one nation of people. Not divided or split apart. That is the army God is raising up slowly amongst us. An empire within an empire. That is what we are becoming slowly. And do not think eyes are not on us. Eyes are on us outside of here, and eyes are on us in here too.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was set down “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and they were “very dry.” A valley full of bones is a graveyard. Very dry means no nourishment, no understanding, no water. David names that same valley: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. The world took the words of the famous Christian prayer and made a song of them, but the valley of the shadow of death is a real place in the scripture.

It is the same darkness Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. It is the same land Baruch spoke of earlier, where our people wax old and are defiled with the dead in a strange land. And it is the same place Isaiah speaks of when the Lord comes to bring out “them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” The valley of dry bones, the valley of the shadow of death, the land of darkness and the prison house are all one place: the lands of our captivity.

So the valley Ezekiel walked round about is where our people are today, dead and dry in a strange land. Yet even there the one who walks with the Lord fears no evil, because the Lord is with him, and it is the Lord who will bring those bones to life.

precepts.text: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. The table is the Bible. Habakkuk 2:2, write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it; Isaiah 30:8, write it before them in a table and note it in a book for the time to come, that this is a rebellious people. We read the tables about what is happening overseas as entertainment while our own spirit is rotten. You are in the greatest place on earth, being taught the future out of these pages, and some of you scorn it.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

precepts.text: A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland; so laying in green pastures is going into peace.
precepts.point: The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. It is going into the homeland, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, Israel.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”. What are these green pastures? Ezekiel tells of the land the Most High espied for us when he brought us out of Egypt: “In the day that I lifted up mine hand unto them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands”.

A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland. The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. So lying down in green pastures is going into peace, going into the homeland, Jerusalem, Israel.

precepts.text: Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; that is the shadow of death, captivity.
precepts.point: The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. The shadow of death is defined here: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron”.

The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron: captivity. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies. Walking through it, we fear no evil, for he is with us, and his rod and his staff comfort us.

precepts.text: Now go, write it before them in a table and note it in a book; the "it" is the words of the Lord, His laws and commandments to get us right.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies”. What is the table? “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

The “it” is the words of the Lord: His laws, statutes and commandments, written in a table and noted in a book to get us right. The table is the word of the Lord written in a book, our correction and our comfort in these last days, prepared before us in the presence of our enemies, the other nations, and more specifically the Edomite nations whose hands are still in America today.

precepts.text: These things hast thou done and I kept silence; but I will reprove thee and set them in order before thine eyes, talking about the other nations.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
How does the Most High prepare the table in the presence of the enemy? By setting them in order before our eyes: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.”

This is talking about the other nations. They do heinous things against us: they kill us, shoot us down, imprison us, put drugs in our neighborhoods and call it a "war on drugs" when they mean war on us, the Israelites. They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings, and thought the Most High was such an one as themselves.

He kept silence, but He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and the comfort, right in the presence of our enemies.

precepts.text: After three days and a half the spirit of life from God entered into them and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them, in the presence of our enemies.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies, and so is the rising: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

The spirit of life from God enters into them and they stand on their feet, and great fear falls on them which saw them. That is in the presence of our enemies. With the book, the correction and comfort of His laws, statutes and commandments, we rise up as a great army before the very nations that killed us, imprisoned us and put drugs in our neighborhoods.
